messages:
sophia.partnerships: Heads-up: Partner CloudX published a new rate-limit/profile that accidentally sets burst=1000 for their marketplace vendor account. That allowed a storm of short-lived reservations that ate ~40% of our dedicated NL pool this morning. Noticed during quota sweep. :confused:
kevin.ops: Wow. We see a spike in allocation-create events from partner_id=cloudx from 07:12-07:21 UTC. Many of them are 1-minute reservations then cancel, but they still reserve capacity. I'm going to throttle partner allocations at the gateway level and enable a partner-specific rate-limit.
martin.hw: We also had started a pre-stage move of 8 racks to NL yesterday. If throttling isn't enough we can pause partner allocations and move 4 racks to the NL-ded pool to stabilize customer SLAs. That would be a 5-7 hour operation to re-provision and network patch.
tara.sales: Affected customers: RapidRetail (promised launch tomorrow) and MedFin (contract commit next week). Both expect reserved throughput. Can Partnerships own the initial comms? They want a concrete mitigation plan, not just "we're looking into it."\sophia.partnerships: I'll draft a short advisory. Kevin, please confirm ETA for throttle rollout and whether it will retroactively free the reservations. We should avoid blaming partner in the customer note.
kevin.ops: Throttle command (ops-only):
```
redwoodctl partners throttle --partner cloudx --burst 5 --rate 20/s --region nl-west --reason "marketplace-burst-misconfig"
```
I'll apply to gateway and put it behind an approval. Expect effect within 90s after apply. It will stop new bursts but won't auto-release already-created short reservations. We'll need reconcile to free them.
infra-bot: approval-needed: throttle request by kevin.ops for partner cloudx; approve with `approve-bot 1234` in this channel.
tara.sales: If reconcile won't auto-release, what's the plan to free capacity now? Customers need reassurance.
kevin.ops: Plan: 1) Apply throttle (ETA 2m). 2) Run allocation reconcile to expire transient reservations older than 3m (we'll treat them as stale):
```
redwoodctl allocations reconcile --region nl-west --stale-threshold 180 --partner cloudx --dry-run
```
Dry-run first, then run for real if output looks safe. 3) If reconcile can't free enough, use Martin's spare racks as short-term swap.
martin.hw: I'll stage 4 racks for rapid swap. If we hit that path, ops needs to coordinate DB rebind and BGP flaps window.
sophia.partnerships: @kevin.ops please proceed with throttle and dry-run reconcile. I'll coordinate the customer note and include a temporary credit offer if we need to migrate their workload. Tara, what's the minimum credit to mention?
tara.sales: Keep it conservative: offer 5% one-off credit for any short SLA breach, escalate to account leads for anything larger. Need clear language about temporary mitigation window.
earlo.ops: (shadow user) Running dry-run reconcile now, output shows ~22 stale reservations that would free ~18% of NL pool capacity. Looks promising.
kevin.ops: Dry-run looks good. Applying throttle and then reconcile for real.
infra-bot: action: throttle request executed by kevin.ops; reconciliation job queued (job id r-1781234000-1).
earlo.ops: Reconcile finished: freed 20 stale reservations; pool utilization back to expected range. No customer allocations lost. Audit saved at /logs/reconcile/1781234000.csv.
martin.hw: Great. I'll keep the 4 racks warm but hold shipping until we confirm no further bursts.
sophia.partnerships: Drafted customer note and shared in DM with Tara for review. Key points: brief cause, what we did (throttle + reconcile), status (capacity normalized), gesture (5% credit if SLA impacted), and contact for escalation.
tara.sales: Reviewed. Send at EOD to affected accounts with ops cc.
sophia.partnerships: Final Actions: 1) Partnerships to send customer advisory at EOD. 2) Ops to leave partner throttle for 24h and monitor. 3) Martin to keep spare racks ready for 48h. 4) Partnerships will request partner action item: fix their marketplace profile and add webhook validation to prevent large bursts. Closing thread unless something changes. :white_check_mark:
